input.summary: Jordan Doe's credentials (EKS role session eks-developer/jdoe@example.com, plus jdoe@example.com on GKE and AKS) were used from 198.51.100.23. That IP belongs to NIGHTOWL-HOSTING (NL) and is flagged malicious on threat feeds as bulletproof hosting, an open docker registry on port 5000 and Kubernetes API brute-forcing. Jordan is on PTO until 10-19 and normally uses a Mac (darwin), but the client here was linux kubectl. The same playbook ran on all three clusters, one after another: EKS at 14:02, GKE at 14:38 and AKS at 15:11. Each run went: permission check, list namespaces, failed attempts on kube-system secrets and jobs (403), read the payments/payments-db-credentials secret, create a privileged pod (debug-tools-7f9c) with hostPID, hostNetwork and the host's root filesystem mounted, then exec into it with nsenter to get a shell on the node. From the node the attacker stole the in-cluster-only argocd-application-controller service account token (cluster-admin) and used it from the same external IP to create ClusterRoleBinding jdoe-break-glass, which gives jdoe cluster-admin. Next they set up persistence in kube-system: DaemonSet kube-metrics-agent and CronJob node-cert-rotate, both pulling images from the attacker's registry at 198.51.100.23:5000. They also created a NodePort service (metrics-agent-np, port 30080) and finally listed secrets across all namespaces, which is the alerted event. All three clusters should be treated as fully compromised: payments DB credentials and every cluster secret are exposed, and the argocd token and jdoe's sessions must be revoked.
